ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE OCCURS WHEN BACTERIA DEVELOP THE ABILITY TO SURVIVE EXPOSURE TO ANTIBIOTICS. THIS IS A NATURAL EVOLUTIONARY PROCESS DRIVEN BY NATURAL SELECTION. **Response:**

Antibiotic resistance arises when bacteria evolve mechanisms to survive exposure to antibiotics. This is driven by natural selection: antibiotics kill susceptible bacteria, but those with genetic mutations or inherited resistance traits survive and reproduce, passing on their resistance. Overprescription accelerates this by frequently exposing bacteria to antibiotics, increasing the likelihood of resistance mutations and favoring resistant strains. This reduces the effectiveness of antibiotics over time.
